STAGE 2|2|0:
Your role

Welcome to the study. You have been assigned to [Vertex/Atlas], a talent organization. Its candidates are people from an earlier study who completed three timed tasks, now put forward for independent review. [Vertex/Atlas] seeks a strong showing against candidates from other organizations and depends on you to speak for them.

As its representative, you speak for [Vertex/Atlas] candidates. Each review compares a [Vertex/Atlas] candidate with one from another organization. You choose how much of $0.50 to place behind the [Vertex/Atlas] candidate. You always back [Vertex/Atlas]; you decide only the amount, so choose what best reflects your judgment.

In a separate study, independent reviewers will see some of your decisions. They decide how far to follow each with their own money and whether they want more of your decisions. Those decisions shape their view of you and [Vertex/Atlas]. Your bonus depends on one of your reviewed decisions, picked at random, so any decision could count.
STAGE 2|3|0:
The candidates

The candidates completed three timed tasks in an earlier paid study: general knowledge, word search, and logical reasoning.

You will see each candidate’s general-knowledge and word-search percentile scores when available. 75th percentile means the candidate performed better than 75% of participants on that task. “Unknown” means only that the score is unavailable.

You will not see the logical-reasoning scores. Please see below for an example of each task.
STAGE 2|5|0:
Making your decisions

The amount you place shows how strongly you vouch for the [Vertex/Atlas] candidate. The amount is your confidence in the referral, and reviewers see it. The more you place, the more of your own pay rises or falls with the candidate’s result.

Each review screen shows the [Vertex/Atlas] candidate on the left and the other candidate on the right, with their available general-knowledge and word-search percentiles. Below them, a slider from 0% to 100% sets how much of your $0.50 you place on the [Vertex/Atlas] candidate. If the [Vertex/Atlas] candidate scored higher, you receive $0.50 plus the amount you placed; if the other candidate scored higher, you receive $0.50 minus the amount you placed.

At 0%, you place $0.00 on [Vertex/Atlas] and receive $0.50 no matter who scored higher.
At 50%, you place $0.25 on [Vertex/Atlas]. If [Vertex/Atlas] scored higher, you receive $0.75; if the other candidate scored higher, you receive $0.25.
At 100%, you place $0.50 on [Vertex/Atlas]. If [Vertex/Atlas] scored higher, you receive $1.00; if the other candidate scored higher, you receive $0.00.

Being right pays you in proportion to how much you placed, and reviewers see how each of your referrals turned out before they decide how far to follow your next one and whether to choose you again.

As you move the slider, the screen shows what you would receive under both outcomes.
STAGE 2|6|0:
Your payment

You get $1.00 for finishing the study. You can also get a bonus of up to $3.00.

Your bonus is based on one of your reviews, picked at random. The bonus has two sources. The first is your own decision: $0.50 plus the amount you placed if the [Vertex/Atlas] candidate scored higher, or $0.50 minus it if the other candidate scored higher. The second part comes from the independent reviewer: how much of their own money they were willing to place behind the candidate you referred, and how much more of your work they said they would want to review. Together, these decisions determine up to $2.00 of your bonus.

You get the bonus after the reviewer study is finished.

Your role

Thank you for participating in our study. You have been assigned the role of independent reviewer. In an earlier study, another participant served as a representative of [Atlas/Vertex], a talent organization, and spoke for its candidates. Each of their decisions compared an [Atlas/Vertex] candidate with one from another organization, and the representative decided how much of $0.50 to place on the [Atlas/Vertex] candidate scoring higher on logical reasoning. They could see the candidates’ scores on two other tasks, when available, but not on logical reasoning. They knew that independent reviewers would later see some of their decisions, and the more they placed, the more of their own pay rode on the candidate.

Your job is to review those decisions. For each one, you will see the representative’s information, the [Atlas/Vertex] candidate’s ID, and the amount placed, and you will decide how far to follow the representative’s call with the $0.50 you receive for each review.
STAGE 3|3|0:
Making your reviews

For each review, you receive a new $0.50. A slider from 0% to 100% sets how much of it you place on the [Atlas/Vertex] candidate. If the [Atlas/Vertex] candidate scored higher, you receive $0.50 plus the amount you placed; if the other candidate scored higher, you receive $0.50 minus the amount you placed. The screen shows what you would receive under both outcomes. Place the amount that best reflects your judgment.

After each review, you learn which candidate scored higher and what you earned. You keep what you earn on every review. These earnings are paid as a bonus on top of your [$X.XX] participation payment.

After your reviews with this representative, you will make one choice about your final review, explained when you reach it, and after that review you will answer two questions about this representative and [Atlas/Vertex]. Your placements and your answers may also add to the representative’s bonus; the choice does not. Your own earnings come from your reviews.

STAGE 3|9|0:
Choose your final representative

Your final review comes from this representative or a different one, drawn at random. You set the chance: 0% means certainly a different one, 100% means certainly this one, and 50% means a coin flip.

The 50% setting costs nothing. Moving away from 50% costs money from your review earnings: a little for a small move and more for a larger move, up to $0.15 at 0% or 100%. The screen shows your setting’s exact cost.

The computer makes one random draw using your chance, deciding who your final review comes from. This choice does not affect the representative’s bonus.
